name: Acadia Parish School System
summary: The district shut down its computer systems on 11 November to investigate a possible network compromise, and told families they would stay offline for the near future. Outside investigators were due on site on 12 November. Classes are continuing, and the district has not said whether any data was accessed or who is behind the incident.

name: Barbour County Schools
summary: After staff received suspicious emails, the district cut internet connectivity across its schools as a precaution and hired outside forensic specialists. The superintendent called it a potential cybersecurity incident and said he knew of no significant threat. Schools stayed open and moved to non-digital teaching; no data exposure or attacker has been reported.

name: Frontline Education
place: Nationwide (K-12 HR and school-health software vendor)
summary: Frontline, a software supplier to school districts, says it found a flaw in a third-party software product in August and that employee records held for customers were exposed. Districts including Methuen, Massachusetts, are notifying staff that addresses, emails and Social Security numbers may be affected. Frontline says it fixed the flaw, hired a cybersecurity firm and contacted law enforcement; no attacker has been named.
peopleNote: people reported affected in breach-notice coverage; mostly school employees

name: Spokane Public Schools
summary: The district learned of a network security incident on 20 September and took payroll, grading and attendance systems offline as a precaution, with teachers recording grades by hand meanwhile. Systems were restored over the following weeks. On 9 October the district said it believes student and staff data was compromised; the number of people and the type of data are not yet known. A leak-site listing by a group called NightSpire on 12 October is an unverified claim.

name: New Plymouth School District
summary: A threat found on the district network led it to stop using computers and cancel classes at all three schools. Families were told to delete suspicious emails that looked like they came from the district.
closure: Classes canceled, due to resume 16 Nov

name: Vanderbilt University
summary: An attack took down university networks, devices and cloud services, and staff and students were told to shut down devices and leave campus WiFi. By 10 November WiFi, email, Brightspace, Zoom and login services were back and classes resumed on the normal schedule, though some systems stayed restricted. A ransomware group called BYOD listed the university on its leak site and made claims about stolen data, which have not been verified. The university says its hospital was not affected.

name: Richmond Public Schools
summary: The district cut internet access across its schools after spotting suspicious activity and taught on paper for days. On 9 Nov it said data taken in the attack may have been posted on the dark web. A forensic audit is under way, a temporary network is in use while a permanent one is rebuilt, and free identity monitoring has reportedly been extended to former students and staff. The FBI and Virginia State Police are investigating.

sources.label: GovTech (stolen data posted to dark web)

peopleNote: students enrolled across 50+ sites (district scale, not a count of people affected)

name: Oneonta City School District
summary: Schools closed on a Friday and the following Monday after life-safety systems were taken offline for the investigation. A group calling itself Shiba ransomware emailed media outlets claiming it stole student, parent and staff records.

name: Jerome School District
summary: Ransomware spread across district servers, taking down communications and door locks. Classes were canceled for two days, then ran on paper and pencil while internet access was restored.

name: Easthampton Public Schools
summary: IT staff saw unknown files appearing on staff desktops and took servers down. A month-long forensic review found no evidence that data was stolen. The district plans to expand multifactor authentication.

name: Springfield Public Schools
summary: An attack that began in mid-August and was found on 5 September, when servers were being encrypted, left about 70 schools without email, phones or records and closed them for four days. A district report to the state, prepared by its attorney, says the attacker is known to the FBI and names Interlock; stolen data was found posted on the dark web in mid-September. Staff and volunteer Social Security numbers are the most sensitive data believed taken, and credit monitoring is being offered. The district says it removed the attacker but is not yet back to full capacity.
peopleNote: students enrolled; number with data exposed not stated
actor: Interlock (per district report to the state)

name: Evanston Township High School
summary: A ransomware attack disrupted district systems, internet and phones. The campus closed for two days, canceling summer classes and sports camps.

name: Delano Public Schools
summary: Ransomware shut down systems across the district and classes were canceled for a day. LockBit claimed the attack in June. The district said it paid nothing.

name: Instructure Canvas
summary: The company behind the Canvas learning platform confirmed a breach of user information and messages. ShinyHunters claimed data on 275 million users at nearly 9,000 schools, a scale Instructure has not verified. Login pages were defaced with a ransom note during finals week, and Instructure said on 12 May that it had reached an agreement with the attackers.
peopleNote: users, claimed by the attackers and unverified

name: Spring Lake Park Schools
summary: Staff shut down every system after finding an outside actor inside the network. Systems needed to run school safely were unavailable, so classes, child care and after-school programs were canceled.

name: Alamo Heights ISD
summary: District systems were down for five days. More than 26,600 Texas residents have since been notified that their data was involved. Qilin claimed the attack.

name: Community College of Beaver County
summary: An attack encrypted college data and cut access to grades, transcripts and financial records. The campus closed, and in-person classes resumed on 30 March. Interlock claimed 780 GB of stolen data.

name: Lehigh Carbon Community College
summary: The college shut all campus sites and moved classes online for more than a week during what it called an IT disruption. The Medusa group later claimed the attack.
closure: Campuses closed more than a week

name: Oakland CUSD 5
summary: The small Coles County district said it was hit by a cyberattack over the winter holiday break and opened an investigation. It later said it refused to pay the ransom the attackers demanded.

name: Denmark School District
summary: A cyber incident left the 1,500-student district without internet for five school days, and teachers went back to paper. The INC Ransom group later listed the district on its leak site and claimed about 70 GB of data. The district has not confirmed data theft.

name: Medinah School District 11
summary: The Qilin ransomware group listed the district on its leak site and threatened to publish data. The district has not publicly confirmed an attack.

name: Lakeside Union School District
summary: The Rhysida ransomware group listed the district on its leak site and threatened to release data. The district has not publicly confirmed an attack.

name: Tulare City School District
summary: The 9,300-student district said it was investigating suspicious activity that disrupted some systems and warned families about suspicious emails. An extortion note signed SingularityMD that threatened to release district records circulated on social media; it has not been verified.

name: Alcorn School District
summary: The district detected suspicious activity and temporarily disabled its network while it investigated. LockBit later claimed the attack.

name: Ohio County Schools
summary: The district lost internet service in what officials called a potential cyberattack, then restored it. Officials did not say what happened or who was responsible.

name: Monmouth University
summary: The university found that an outside party had accessed its data and later confirmed a breach. The PEAR group claimed it took 16 TB. Breach notices are still going out, with about 1,500 people confirmed so far across four states.

name: Wagon Mound Public Schools
summary: The tiny district of about 70 students took its internet and networked computers offline after the superintendent told families the system was infected. Interlock claimed about 80 GB of staff and student data.

name: Hanover County Public Schools
summary: Internet service and several systems went down across the 17,000-student division, and teaching moved offline. Investigators later tied the outage to an attempted ransomware attack, and the division confirmed that personal information of students and staff may have been exposed.

name: San Felipe-Del Rio CISD
summary: Most in-network systems, including internet and phones, went down after the district detected suspicious activity. Schools stayed open while systems were restored. The district has not confirmed ransomware or data theft.

name: Belgrade School District
summary: Malware disrupted district technology in early April and affected routine school functions for weeks. The district was still restoring systems in late May and reviewing whether data was exposed.

name: Kentwood Public Schools
summary: The district said Wi-Fi went down across its schools after a student used malicious software built to interfere with the network.

name: San Diego Community College District
summary: The district shut down its network across City, Mesa and Miramar colleges and its continuing education college after detecting an attack. Websites, email, Wi-Fi and registration were offline for about two weeks, and some offices closed. The district says no personal information is confirmed stolen.

name: Onslow County Schools
summary: Phones and internet went down at every site in the 28,000-student district during graduation week. The district later said a criminal group known for similar attacks worldwide was responsible and spent the following weeks rebuilding its network.

name: Cedar Crest College
summary: The college confirmed a ransomware attack in July. The NightSpire group claimed responsibility.

name: Sumner County Schools
summary: A breach of the district network led the school board to push the first day of school back and postpone registration. More than a week later, parents had not been told what data was involved.
closure: First day moved from 4 Aug to 10 Aug

name: Salida Union School District
summary: The Qilin ransomware group listed the district on its leak site. The district has not publicly confirmed an attack.

name: Oceanside Unified School District
summary: Staff lost email, internet, Google Drive and district applications in the weeks before the school year began. The district confirmed a network disruption, and a district text message described it as a cyberattack.

name: Upland Unified School District
summary: The SafePay ransomware group claimed an attack on the district. The district has not publicly confirmed it.

name: DC Public Schools
summary: Attackers got into a web application used for summer learning and after-school registration. Student names, birth dates, home addresses and parent contact details from 55 schools may have been exposed. The ExfilSquad group claimed the attack and about 60,000 records.

name: Newton County Schools
summary: Unauthorized activity knocked out district systems and applications days before the school year started, and disruptions lasted more than a week. The FBI joined the investigation. Qilin claimed the attack in late August.

name: Southeastern Oklahoma State University
summary: The university pulled computers offline and closed its physical campus for three days after a cybersecurity incident. Interlock later claimed it stole 710 GB of data.

name: Brazosport College
summary: A ransomware attack disrupted college services in August. Most were back after about 10 days. Qilin claimed responsibility.

name: Tulare Joint Union High School District
summary: The district was hit in August, and a group calling itself Booba Project claimed 35 GB of data. The district began mailing breach notices in October. The number of people affected has not been released.

name: University of Texas at San Antonio
summary: The university took phones, registration and payment systems offline after detecting unauthorized activity days before the fall semester. The start of classes for more than 42,000 students slipped by three days. The university says the activity was stopped before it reached core systems.
closure: Semester start moved from 19 Aug to 24 Aug

name: Battle Creek Public Schools
summary: The Rhysida ransomware group claimed an attack on the district. The district has not publicly confirmed it.

name: Westfield Public Schools
summary: A district-wide network outage began on the first day of school, and disruptions continued for about two weeks. INC Ransom listed the district on its leak site the next day.

name: North Slope Borough School District
summary: A September attack disrupted the district phone system. The district has begun sending breach notices; the number of people affected is not known. INC Ransom claimed the attack.

name: Slate Valley Unified School District
summary: The Kairos group said it stole 762 GB from the district in September. The district confirmed that it did not meet the ransom demand.

name: Sutton Public Schools
summary: A September attack hit both the school district and the Town of Sutton. A group called Global claimed 533 GB of data.

name: Llano ISD
summary: The district confirmed a cybersecurity incident at the end of September and took some systems offline. Qilin claimed the attack.
